classification.difficultyReason: Identify equal angles using parallel lines and vertically opposite angles, then apply a congruence test with matching vertices.

content.prompt: In the diagram, $PQ\parallel ST$ and $QR=SR$. Prove that triangles $PQR$ and $TSR$ are congruent.

spec.description: Crossed triangles with P and Q above S and T. PT and SQ intersect at R. Matching arrows mark horizontal PQ and ST as parallel; single ticks mark QR and SR as equal. Ordinary source blue geometry is rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: P, R, T are collinear; S, R, Q are collinear; PQ is parallel to ST; QR equals SR.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied geometry, labels, parallel arrows and equality ticks are visible.

answer.short:
$\triangle PQR\equiv\triangle TSR$ (AAS).

Alternate angles and vertically opposite angles give two matching angle pairs; $QR=SR$ is given.
answer.worked:
In $\triangle PQR$ and $\triangle TSR$,

$\angle PQR=\angle TSR$ (alternate angles, $PQ\parallel ST$),

$\angle PRQ=\angle TRS$ (vertically opposite angles),

$QR=SR$ (given).

Therefore, $\triangle PQR\equiv\triangle TSR$ (AAS).
